speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you're here to discuss weakness and fatigue; to help narrow this down, have these symptoms been present for a long time or did they start suddenly? Additionally, have you noticed any changes in your weight, appetite, or sleep patterns recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 33-year-old woman. The patient reports feeling extremely fatigued and weak, especially towards the end of the day, to the point of difficulty in self-care. She mentions experiencing these symptoms currently. The patient has been traveling, hiking, and camping recently and notes having had multiple illnesses in the recent past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent travel, hiking, camping, and multiple illnesses, have you experienced fever, chills, or night sweats, and do you have any specific rashes or joint pain? Also, what specific foods do you consume daily?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness and fatigue. I also have Mild diplopia. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of profound fatigue, weakness affecting daily self-care, and mild diplopia (double vision) is highly characteristic of this neuromuscular disorder, rather than a urinary tract infection. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies, REQUEST TEST: Repetitive Nerve Stimulator Study, REQUEST IMAGES: Chest CT to evaluate for thymoma.
